signal: A runtime signal — such as a guardrail flagging a data-exfiltration attempt or an agent's unauthorised-tool-call rate crossing a threshold — starts the flow.
detect: Runtime detection comes from observability and guardrails.
drill: The kill switch is tested on a schedule — the pull is drilled monthly — because an untested kill switch is not a control.
breaker: A circuit breaker at the tool-call boundary trips on a defined signal — a threshold breach, an anomaly, or a manual pull.
revoke: Tripping revokes just that agent's scope and halts its tool calls.
fleet: Containment stops one agent without breaking the rest of the fleet, which keeps running.
triage: Runtime detection is wired to a triage workflow that classifies severity.
decision: Triage decides whether the event is reportable against the severity criteria.
incident: A reportable event opens an incident and starts the statutory timer, encoding the EU AI Act Art. 73 timeline.
report: The report is drafted against the required template and pre-filled from the trace and registry entry.
record: The incident record is held as machine-readable evidence.
notify: The pipeline turns the runtime signal into a reported obligation delivered within the legal window.
